title: 6 - Legend

[INTRODUCTION TEXT]

## 7.1. Create the legend container

We want our map legend to explain what the symbols and colours on the map represent. We will place a legend in the top-right corner of the map.

The legend consists of two parts: 
- In `index.html`, we define the HTML elements and the text that users will see. 
- In `style.css`, we define the position and appearance of the legend and its items.

- [ ] First, add the basic legend container to the HTML file.

```html
<!-- Map legend -->
      <div id="legend">
        Some stuff for our legend.
    </div>
```

Save the `index.html` file and preview the changes on your webmap. See the small text in the upper-right corner? That's your legend (for now)!

- [ ] Next, open your `style.css` file. Add the following code block to the end of the existing code:

```css
/* ----------------------------------------
    Legend
---------------------------------------- */
#legend {
  position: absolute;
  top: 0;
  right: 0;
  z-index: 10;
  margin-top: 10px;
  margin-right: 10px;
  background: white;
  opacity: 0.95;
  border-radius: 5px;
  box-shadow: 0 2px 6px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.25);
  padding: 5px 10px;
}

#legend p {
  margin: 10px 0 5px;
}

.legend-item {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 8px;
  margin: 5px 0;
}
```

Here, the `#legend {` defines how the legend container looks like - a white box with some shadow and other tweaks. `z-index: 10` makes sure the legend is written on top of the map.

`#legend p {` on the other hand defines how the normal paragraph text inside the legend will be spaced.

`.legend-item {}` defines placement of the coloe boxes that match with our layers' visualisation.


## 7.2. Add symbols for the map layers

The legend needs a symbol and a label for each category. We will use small coloured boxes for the forest reserve categories and patterned boxes for national parks and international conservation areas.

In `index.html`, add a legend item for each category. Each item contains a symbol element and a text label. In `style.css`, use classes to define the appearance of the symbols.

```html
<!-- Map legend -->
      <div id="legend">

        <!-- Basemap selection -->
        <p><strong>Basemap</strong></p>

        <label class="basemap-option">
          <input type="radio" name="basemap" value="osm" checked>
          OpenStreetMap
        </label>

        <label class="basemap-option">
          <input type="radio" name="basemap" value="satellite">
          MapTiler Satellite
        </label>

        <hr>

        <!-- Forest reserve layers -->
        <p><strong>Forest reserves</strong></p>

        <div class="legend-item">
          <span class="legend-swatch forest-reserve"></span>
          Forest reserve
        </div>

        <div class="legend-item">
          <span class="legend-swatch forest-plantation"></span>
          Forest plantation
        </div>

        <div class="legend-item">
          <span class="legend-swatch nature-reserve"></span>
          Nature forest reserve
        </div>

        <div class="legend-item">
          <span class="legend-swatch village-reserve"></span>
          Village land forest reserve
        </div>

        <p><strong>National parks and conservation areas</strong></p>

        <!-- Conservation area layers -->
        <div class="legend-item">
          <span class="legend-swatch national-park"></span>
          National park
        </div>

        <div class="legend-item">
          <span class="legend-swatch international-area"></span>
          International conservation area
        </div>

      </div>
    </div>
```
Save and preview.


The class names connect the HTML elements to their CSS styles. For example, the `forest-reserve` class applies the colour defined by `.forest-reserve` in the `style.css` stylesheet.

Make sure the legend colours and patterns match the styles you created in Chapter 5. If you change a layer's style, update its legend symbol as well.

- [ ] Copy the following CSS code and paste it at the end of your `style.css` file:

```css
/* ----------------------------------------
    Legend symbols (match with layer visualisation)
---------------------------------------- */
/* Forest reserve categories */
.forest-reserve {
  background: #006b00;
}

.forest-plantation {
  background: #d3f226;
}

.nature-reserve {
  background: #81bf00;
}

.village-reserve {
  background: #56cf68;
}
/* National parks layer */
.national-park {
  background: repeating-linear-gradient(
    45deg,
    #000000,
    #000000 1px,
    transparent 1px,
    transparent 7px
  );
  border: 1px solid #000000;
}

/* International conservation areas layer */
.international-area {
  background: repeating-linear-gradient(
    135deg,
    #000000,
    #000000 1px,
    transparent 1px,
    transparent 7px
  );
  border: 1px solid #000000;
}
```
